confirmed.title: Just-added player row is never saved — vanishes on reload while every other setup edit persists
repro: Open https://music-timeline-walksalots-projects.vercel.app/index.html?debug=1 with cleared localStorage
Tap New game (roster shows the default 4 rows)
Tap '+ Add player' once (roster shows 5 rows)
Touch nothing else, wait 2+ seconds (past every debounce), reload the page
Tap New game again: roster is back to 4 rows
confirmed.expected: The added seat survives reload like every other setup edit (mode, target, stake, Venmo handle, removed rows, and typed names all persist in the same session).
confirmed.actual: The added row is gone; the 'add-player' action calls only render() and never queues or fires a save, so no wait duration helps.
sources: setup-options:A just-added player row silently vanishes on reload — 'Add player' is the only setup control that never persists
confirmed.rationale: Single report, no merge. Not S1 data loss: only an unnamed default seat in pre-game setup is lost — typed names, removals, and started games persist, so no saved game/roster/stake meaningfully vanishes. Not S2: the add-player feature itself works; only its persistence is missing. S3 fits: silent, janky-but-recoverable state loss (family can re-add the seat), with a real impact window (tab discard during setup silently drops a seat). Reporter's S4 undersells a silent-loss inconsistency; distinct from round-3's pagehide-flush race since no save is ever queued at all.

v1.reason: Reproduced exactly as written against the live production site in a fresh browser session (script: scratch/qa/round-5/verify-add-player-row-not-persisted-1/verify.mjs, run from repo root; screenshots 01-06 in that dir). With cleared localStorage: New game shows 4 rows, + Add player shows 5, after a 2.5s wait (debounce is 500ms) and reload the roster is back to 4 — and localStorage held no players key at all before the reload, so no save was ever queued. Both contrast claims verified: add+type-name+reload keeps 5 rows (debounced keystroke path saves the roster), and remove+reload persists the removal. Source confirms the mechanism: the 'add-player' handler in public/music/ui.js line 4240 only pushes the draft and calls render() — no rememberRoster() and no queued save — while 'remove-player' (line 4249) calls rememberRoster() and name input goes through the debounced rememberRoster() path. Not in the brief's by-design list. Severity: not S1 (nothing saved vanishes — the seat was never saved; named rosters and started games survive), not S2 (the feature works in-session; only persistence is missing), and beyond S4 polish since it is a silent functional persistence gap inconsistent with every sibling setup control. S3 "janky-but-recoverable flow" fits: one tap restores the unnamed seat, with a real loss window (tab discard mid-setup).

confirmed.title: In-game menu (rules / End game) unreachable from reveal and pass screens — ending early forces starting the next player's turn
repro: Fresh page -> New game -> Skip photo on every row -> pick any mode -> Shuffle & start
Tap the pass hand-off, place the card, land on the reveal screen
Try to open the menu: no menu control exists on the reveal or pass screens
The only #btn-menu lives inside section#play, so you must tap Next player and the pass hand-off — drawing the next card and starting the next song — before End game is reachable
confirmed.expected: Rules and End game are reachable from the reveal and pass screens; stopping the game or checking a rule at the verdict moment should not require advancing into another player's turn.
confirmed.actual: index.html has exactly one data-action="open-menu" control (inside the play statusbar); the reveal section has no statusbar and the pass statusbar shows only turn/progress, so ending requires a turn-advance or a reload -> Home -> Resume.
sources: coop:In-game menu (rules / End game) is unreachable from the reveal and pass screens — ending early requires starting another player's turn
confirmed.rationale: Single report, no merge. Not by-design and not an a11y trap (no S2): the controls exist and work from the play screen, and reload->Home->Resume is a full workaround, so no feature dead-ends. It is exactly the rubric's S3 'janky-but-recoverable flow': a table stopping mid-game must burn a turn-advance that audibly starts the next song. Raised from the reporter's S4 because this is a flow defect a family hits at a predictable moment (disputes happen at the reveal), not mere polish.

v1.reason: Reproduced live in my own Chrome session against the production URL (seed=42, fresh localStorage), UI-only, script at scratch/qa/round-5/verify-menu-unreachable-from-reveal-pass-1/verify.mjs with screenshots 01-08. Static check first: index.html has exactly one data-action="open-menu" control (#btn-menu, line 859) and it sits inside section#play; ui.js binds open-menu to nothing else and has no keyboard route. Live: on the pass screen the ONLY visible interactive control is #btn-pass-continue (statusbar shows just turn/progress, screenshot 01); on the reveal screen the only visible controls are the roster seats (all show-scoreboard), and #btn-next-player (screenshot 03) — zero visible open-menu/show-rules/end-game controls on either, menu-sheet stays data-open=false. I exhausted the side route the finding had to survive: roster seat -> scoreboard offers only "Back to the game", no menu/rules/end. The forced cost is real and I measured it: tapping Next player -> pass hand-off advanced state to turn 2 AND audibly started the next song (audio element paused:false, currentTime 1.08s, real audio-ssl.itunes.apple.com src) before #btn-menu became reachable; opening it there shows End game and How to play working. The claimed workaround also verified: reload lands on home with the Resume card visible, so nothing dead-ends. Severity: not S2 — no feature is broken, no control is hidden or trapped, the game survives, and recovery is one reload; exactly the rubric's S3 "janky-but-recoverable flow" — stopping or checking a rule at the dispute-prone reveal moment forces starting another player's turn with an audible new song, which a family hits predictably. Not in the brief's by-design list and no design comment claims the omission is intentional. S3 stands as proposed.

repro: Open https://music-timeline-walksalots-projects.vercel.app/index.html?debug=1 with cleared localStorage
New game, open the 'Deck & playback' foldout
Set 'Play songs with' to 'Spotify (QR link)'
Fold the panel and read the summary line
confirmed.expected: The collapsed line reflects everything switched on inside the foldout (per the app's own markup comment), so a non-default playback source appears in the summary.
confirmed.actual: The folded line reads only 'All decades · all genres · 1185 songs' — deck filters update it, playback source does not, so a table persisted on Spotify looks identical to the in-app-preview default until the first card plays silence.
sources: setup-options:Folded 'Deck & playback' summary hides a non-default playback source — Spotify/Apple/YouTube mode leaves no trace once folded
confirmed.rationale: Single report, no merge. An incomplete summary line rather than actively false copy: one tap (unfold) reveals the true setting, nothing is hidden from the controls themselves, and the moment audio does not play the Spotify flow presents itself. Subtle inconsistency with the panel's own stated contract — S4 polish, matching the reporter.

v1.reason: Reproduced exactly as written in a fresh Playwright Chrome session (viewport 393x852, empty localStorage) against the live site. New game -> opened 'Deck & playback' foldout -> selected 'Spotify (QR link)' in the #playback-source select -> refolded: the summary line #setup-more-state still read verbatim 'All decades · all genres · 1185 songs' (screenshot 03-folded-spotify.png), with no trace of the playback source. The asymmetry is real: dropping one decade chip immediately changed the same folded line to '7 decades · all genres · 1059 songs' (04-folded-filter.png). I also closed the two refutation angles: (1) the setting genuinely sticks — after fold+unfold the select still reads 'spotify' and localStorage music-timeline:v1:settings persists playbackSource:"spotify", so a persisted-on-Spotify table really is indistinguishable from the preview default while folded; (2) source confirms mechanism, not accident of timing — ui.js:1712-1736 builds the summary from decades/genres/eligible-count only, while the playback select lives inside the same foldout (index.html:753-773), and the markup comment at index.html:691-694 explicitly promises 'folding hides the controls, never what is actually switched on', so it contradicts the app's own stated contract and is not on the brief's by-design list. Severity stays S4 per the rubric: the line is incomplete rather than false, no control is hidden, one tap reveals the truth, and the Spotify flow announces itself the moment a card plays — subtle inconsistency/polish, matching the reporter's proposal. Evidence: scratch/qa/round-5/verify-folded-summary-hides-playback-source-1/ (verify.mjs + 4 screenshots), zero page errors.

confirmed.title: 320px winner name sheds an orphan letter for 16-char unbroken names despite the deployed single-line clamp fix
repro: Fresh page: https://music-timeline-walksalots-projects.vercel.app/index.html?debug=1&seed=912
New game; reduce to 2 players; name Player 1 'Konstantinopolis' (16 chars), Player 2 'Bo'; Skip photo on both
Set 'First to' to 5; Shuffle & start; play correct placements (read __timeline.state for a legal gap) until Konstantinopolis wins
On the win screen, set viewport 320x568 and inspect the winner title
confirmed.expected: Per the deployed round-5 fix's own CSS comment, a worst-case 16-char maxlength name renders on one line at the 320px floor.
confirmed.actual: 'Konstantinopoli' plus a lone centred 's' on a second line: the tuned font resolves to 29.38px, at which the name measures 260px against the 254px available; any unbroken 16-char name measuring ~255-290px reproduces. Nothing clips or overflows; multi-word names wrap cleanly.
sources: responsive:320px winner name still sheds an orphan letter when a 16-char unbroken name wins, despite the deployed single-line clamp fix
confirmed.rationale: Single report, no merge. Cosmetic only at the smallest supported viewport, in a narrow band of unbroken name widths; no clipping, no hidden controls, payout and game unaffected, and the designed overflow-wrap fallback still catches extreme names. The contradiction is with an internal CSS comment, not user-facing copy. S4 polish, matching the reporter — but worth keeping since it shows the round-5 fix's stated worst case is not actually covered.

v1.reason: Reproduced on the live site with the exact filed steps (seed 912, UI-only clicks, Konstantinopolis wins first-to-5; then 320x568): the winner title renders 'Konstantinopoli' plus a lone centred 's' on a second line — per-character rect measurement shows 2 line boxes, full text 255.08px vs 254px available, no clipping, no overflow, no console errors (evidence in scratch/qa/round-5/verify-win-name-orphan-letter-320px-1/: measurement.json, 03-win-320x568.png). One correction: the finding's cited numbers are stale — the deployed CSS has been retuned since filing from the cited 10.4vw-3.9px (29.38px/260px) to clamp(24px, 10.88vw - 6.02px, 42px), resolving to 28.796px at 320px — yet the orphan still reproduces, now by a ~1.1px miss, and the deployed comment still claims the worst-case 16-char name fits on one line at the 320px floor. Not on the by-design list; cosmetic only at the smallest supported viewport with game, controls, and payout unaffected, matching the reporter's S4.

confirmed.title: Play-screen status line reads 'Playing the preview.' while the preview is paused
repro: Fresh page: https://music-timeline-walksalots-projects.vercel.app/index.html?debug=1&seed=707
New game -> Skip photo for all 4 players -> Shuffle & start -> tap the pass screen
Wait ~2s for the preview to auto-play (vinyl shows Pause)
Tap the vinyl (#btn-play-song) once to pause
confirmed.expected: The status line under the vinyl reflects the paused state (or goes neutral), matching the vinyl button's own state.
confirmed.actual: audio.paused=true, countdown frozen, button label flips to 'Play song', but the line still reads 'Playing the preview.' (reproduced on seeds 606 and 707).
sources: perf-network:Play-screen status copy still says "Playing the preview." while the preview is paused
confirmed.rationale: Single report, no merge. The line does state a falsehood — borderline S3 'misleading copy' — but the truth is stated immediately adjacent (button label 'Play song', frozen countdown), no action or game outcome is affected, and the worst impact is a moment of second-guessing on a loud phone. That is a wording/state inconsistency, not copy that misleads a player into anything: S4, matching the reporter.

v1.reason: Reproduced exactly as written in fresh real-Chrome sessions (AAC "probably") on both seeds 707 and 606: with the preview audibly playing (currentTime 1.51s advancing), one tap on #btn-play-song pauses (audio.paused=true, currentTime and 29s countdown frozen, label flips to "Play song", aria-pressed=false) while #audio-status still reads "Playing the preview." at t+0.7s and t+2.2s. Source confirms it is structural: ui.js sets the status on the started branches (lines 2345/2381) but the pause path (~line 2316) writes no status. Severity stays S4 per the rubric: the falsehood sits directly beside the truth (play triangle, frozen countdown, the label the user's own tap produced), affects no action, rule outcome, or announcement (aria-live text never changes on pause) — a wording/state inconsistency, not misleading copy that induces anything. Evidence in scratch/qa/round-5/verify-paused-status-copy-says-playing-1/ (repro.mjs + 7 screenshots).

coverage.coverage: First-run & home-screen lane, live site (https://music-timeline-walksalots-projects.vercel.app), real Chrome, ~15 min of scripted-human testing under scratch/qa/round-5/first-run/ (7 scripts, all screenshots reviewed). VERIFIED CLEAN: (1) Fresh visitor after localStorage.clear(): no resume card, no storage warning, deck stat reads "1185 songs · 1950-2025" (matches the Puff-dedupe count). (2) Home at 320x568, 393x852, 768x1024, 1450x1100 and 852x393 landscape: zero horizontal overflow, both buttons reachable, screenshots inspected. (3) How-to-play read end to end (text saved to rules-text.txt): every rule statement matches the brief (turn flow, ties legal, 2-8 players, 2 tokens cap 5 / co-op pool 6, challenge -1 / name-it +1 / buy-card -3, one challenge per player per turn, closest-to-left tiebreak, deck-out -> longest timeline -> tokens -> shared win, four modes, streak bonus, buy-in never charges); no typos; renders cleanly at 393 and 320; close returns home. (4) Resume: mid-turn game (seed 77, preview played, gap tapped) -> reload -> home card "Turn 1 - Alice, Bob, Carmen, Dev" -> resume restored screen, active player, names, tokens, timelines, deck count (1180), mode/target, and even the mid-turn gap selection ("Placing before 1972", Place here enabled). (5) manifest.json 200 application/json with 3 icons all 200 and correct content-types; icon.svg + apple-touch-icon.png 200. (6) Service worker registered/activated/controlling; second visit via reload AND a fresh SW-controlled tab both load and work. (7) Menu sheet (exists only on the play screen - confirmed exactly one open-menu button in the DOM, so "every screen" = play): every row verified - Scoreboard shows correct standings and returns to play; How to play opens rules and returns to play; all four toggles flip via label tap and persist across reload+resume; Reduce motion sets body[data-motion=reduce] live and clears on untoggle; playback-source select has the 4 documented options; Home keeps the game saved; End game is a 2-tap armed control that disarms after ~4s and ends to an honest "Level when it ended" screen; done and the scrim both close the sheet; Tab focuses menu rows. (8) Finished-game record (round-4 fix): "See final result" reopens the final screen; Play again prefills setup with the same players; backing out and reloading keeps the record; only a genuine Shuffle & start replaces it with the live game. Also: returning-family setup pre-skips photos (rows remembered as skipped, start enabled immediately). Zero pageerror/console-error events in every session. NOT COVERED (other lanes or out of time): audio playback depth, reveal auto-advance/challenge/gameplay flows, listen.html, offline mode, real photo uploads, the Played-before edit/forget UI, multi-tab stale overlay. One candidate finding was self-refuted: a "start button stuck disabled" repro turned out to be my script toggling already-skipped photo rows back to unskipped - the Skip photo control is a deliberate aria-pressed toggle and the start button names the block, so it was not reported.

Roster/setup lane, ~15 min of scripted real-UI testing against the live Vercel site in real Chrome (7 Playwright sessions, scripts + screenshots in scratch/qa/round-5/roster/). Tested: player bounds 2-8 (remove disabled at 2 with honest title, add disabled at 8, live tally); placeholder minting after remove/add churn (no duplicate Player N); Skip photo toggle (aria-pressed + status flip both directions); start blocked with photos outstanding (disabled button + honest counting copy that hides when satisfied); real PNG photo pick via the row's file input (thumbnail, Photo added, carried to pass/play/scoreboard); non-image file honestly rejected via toast; avatar library round trip (offered under the typed name on another row, after row removal, and after reload; 'Previous <name> photos' label; people chips carry saved photos); guest list chips (appear after first named game, pre-seat remembered roster, 'already playing' note, chip tap reuses untouched rows with 'Cleo added.' announcement, true full-table state shows disabled chip + 'table is full' note, edit-mode toggle with aria-pressed and hint swap, two-tap armed forget with visible ring and 4s disarm timeout, forget persists across reload, forget unreachable outside edit mode); name edges (40 chars clamps to 16 with visible 16/16 counter, emoji initial renders whole emoji, whitespace-only name shows '?' and starts as Player N, placeholders never remembered as people, duplicate 'Sam'+'Sam' starts and tracks as separate players); roster carry-through verified on pass screen, play rail, __timeline.state, and Standings; no horizontal overflow at 320px on setup/pass/play/scoreboard; zero console errors and zero pageerrors across all sessions. Not tested (out of lane or out of time): photo picks from very large/EXIF-rotated images, duplicate-name ambiguity deep in challenge flows, mid-game rename (not a feature), and the round-5 reveal/auto-advance surfaces owned by other lanes. Several near-findings were run down and proven by-design (stale hidden reason text, enabled chip at 8 seats with untouched rows, single-tap forget being an arm step, chip/cross adjacency in edit mode) — reporting zero defects is the honest result.

~16 minutes of live testing against the production Vercel site in real Chrome (channel: chrome), 393x852 mobile viewport, via 6 throwaway Playwright scripts in scratch/qa/round-5/setup-options/ (r5-1-breadth, r5-2-deck-playback, r5-3-warning-game, r5-4-draft-overflow, r5-5-add-player-persist, r5-6-evidence-playback), all UI-driven with pageerror/console-error wiring — zero errors recorded across every run. Verified passing: all 4 mode rows select + describe correctly; mistake stepper co-op-only, clamped 1-9 with disabled buttons at both ends; target stepper 5/10/15 with exact session-hint arithmetic (co-op hint uses 1 seat); streak toggle on/off; buy-in switch, $ stepper clamped at $0 and $100, pot line exact at every player count from 2 to 8 while adding and removing rows; Venmo field accepts full profile URL / account.venmo.com/u / @handle (extracting the handle) and rejects venmo.com/code, venmo.com/pay, garbage, with correct aria-invalid and hint tones; full 2-player target-5 game with $3 stake and a pasted venmo.com URL — winner screen shows Pot $6, 'Send it to @jane-doe23', working QR, and the Open Venmo button builds venmo.com/jane-doe23?txn=pay&amount=3.00 (correct per-loser amount); deck foldout eligible-count arithmetic matches the live deck data exactly (1185 baseline; 1950s=126; 1950s+jazz=14); the deployed deck is 1185 cards with ZERO duplicate artist+title pairs (exact and parenthetical-stripped normalization; 'Puff, the Magic Dragon' appears exactly once) — the round-5 Puff-dedupe claim holds; thin-deck warning appears exactly when eligible < seats*target+10 with honest copy; zero-deck shows red '0 songs match' and a disabled Shuffle & start with 'Not enough songs match these filters'; All-chips restore idempotent; last-chip-off re-presses the whole group (verified as by-design in code after my script initially misread it); playback select defaults to preview with 4 options; folded summary tracks deck filters; setup draft (mode/target/streak/stake/venmo) restores after reload; no horizontal overflow at 320px or 393px with foldout open and buy-in on, nor on the win screen. Not covered (out of my lane or out of time): reveal auto-advance/vote-chip/challenge-pill/desktop-rail newest-surface items (other lanes), Play-again record retention (other lane; my win screen did offer 'Play again — same players'), photo capture flows, and a garbage-handle-into-game winner-screen rerun (round-4 verified it; validation behavior unchanged this round).

Two full classic games plus three focused probes against the live site (all real Chrome, AAC decode confirmed, iPhone-ish 393x852 unless noted; scripts and screenshots in scratch/qa/round-5/classic-game/). GAME 1 (2 players to 5, honest placement, seed 551001): pass screens named the right player with correct N/target progress; single pass-tap drew the card AND started audible playback (currentTime advancing, verified on 3 cards); selected gap visibly widens with a pink dashed marker plus a 'Placing before 1970' caption; reveal showed correct year/title/artist/verdict/strip on every turn; every honest placement judged correct; win fired exactly at 5 (not early/late) with winner, sorted timeline chips, decade recap, confetti; no horizontal overflow on pass/win. NEW round-5 auto-advance contract verified end to end: on a plain reveal the Next button arms with data-autonext and aria-label 'Next player — advancing automatically', the polite live region (#live-status) announced 'Next player in 15 seconds — tap anywhere to stay.'; a tap on the verdict banner (no data-action element) cancelled it — armed state cleared and the reveal was still up 16.5s later; on an untouched reveal the timer fired at ~15s and advanced to the next pass screen; the drain animation renders on the button. GAMES 1b/1c (seeds 551002/551003): the finished game's record survived Play again byte-identical, survived a reload during post-game setup (home shows a 'See final result — Game over — Maja, Finn' resume card that reopens the win screen with the same winner), and was genuinely replaced only by Shuffle & start (game-over/turn-7 record became turn-start/turn-1 with 1-card timelines); roster and photo-skip state persisted through Play again AND reload. GAME 2 (4 players to 10, deliberate miss every 3rd turn, seed 552002, 45 turns, 33 hits/12 misses): strict round-robin turn order never broke; roster rail active/next/leader flags matched state on every turn; pass and play progress counters matched timelines; every miss discarded exactly one card whose id landed in the discard pile, timeline unchanged, 'belongs' line correctly hidden on discarded cards and shown on kept ones; mid-game scoreboard via menu was correct (standings sorted, 'up now' on the right seat, token dots, year chips, deck-remaining arithmetic 1185-4-10=1171 exact) and Back returned to play with the same card; win fired exactly at 10 with the other three at 9; Play again returned to setup with all four names. All scripts and evidence under scratch/qa/round-5/perf-network/. (1) COLD visit, fresh profile: load 1087ms (DCL 379ms), 19 page-target requests, 18 network hits, 428.7 KB transferred; including SW precache (captured via PW_EXPERIMENTAL_SERVICE_WORKER_NETWORK_EVENTS context events) total ~518.6 KB / 46 requests — the extra ~90 KB is the SW precaching files the page didn't load (listen.html/listen.js/listen.css, latin-ext fonts, apple-touch-icon), NOT a double download: sw.js install uses cache:'default' on first install so it reuses the HTTP cache (verified in live sw.js source and by byte totals). Zero 4xx/5xx, zero failed requests, nothing fetched twice over the network at page target. Largest assets: previews.json 137.8 KB wire (477 KB raw, compressed), ui.js 54.2 KB, deck.js 40.5 KB, index.html 26.7 KB, fonts ~15-25 KB each. SW cache music-timeline-v14-qa4-record installed with 28 entries. (2) WARM reload: 536ms, ZERO network hits at page target — all 18 app files served fromServiceWorker (CDP responseReceived.fromServiceWorker=true), performance resource entries all transferSize=0. The SW's 18 background revalidations use fetch cache:'no-cache'; Vercel serves etags + max-age=0,must-revalidate, and a conditional request measured 304/0 bytes — so warm wire cost is ~18 tiny 304s, by design (stale-while-revalidate documented in sw.js). (3) OFFLINE reload after one online visit: succeeds in ~30ms, full home renders with an \"offline ok\" badge, New game visible and tappable, 18/19 requests from SW, zero failures (03-offline-home.png). (4) AUDIO: preview auto-plays on entering the play screen — HTTP 206 from audio-ssl.itunes.apple.com, ~1106 KB fetched in ~380ms, currentTime advances with paused=false; the vinyl is a play/pause toggle (labels flip Pause/Play song) and Replay restarts playback correctly (verified playing at 2.42s). Checked across 5 cards on 3 seeds; audio is never cached (network-only, by design). My first probe misread the toggle as a playback failure — perf3/perf4 disproved that; no audio finding. (5) CPU THROTTLE 4x (Emulation.setCPUThrottlingRate): full setup->play->place->reveal flow completed; every step under 1.8s (home->setup 133ms, skip photos 17ms, shuffle->pass 1730ms, pass->play 574ms, tap-play->gaps 377ms, place->reveal 182ms) — nothing approaches unusable. (6) Zero console errors and zero pageerrors across every session (cold, warm, offline, audio x2, throttled).
